svg.text: The SMART Study · set-up guide
Route A: Your child has an iPhone, and you have an iPhone or iPad
Put your child in your family
group
5 minutes · on your phone
1. On your phone, open Settings and tap your name at
the very top.
2. Tap Family.
3. Tap Add Member (or the +), then follow the prompts
to add your child.
4. – If your child already has their own Apple Account,
choose Invite Others and invite that account.
5. – If they don't have one, choose Create Child
Account.
6. Check the date of birth is correct. The phone uses
your child's age to decide which protections apply
automatically. A wrong birth year quietly switches
off protections you think you have.
7. To check you're over 18, you may be asked for a
credit card, or the security code (CVV) of the card
on your Apple Account. It's only an ID check and you
won't be charged, but without a credit card Apple
won't let you create a child account.

svg.text: Sign your child's iPhone in
to their account
5 minutes · on your child's phone
1. If their iPhone is signed in to someone else's
account, such as yours or an old one, sign out of it
first: Settings → the name at the top → Sign Out.
2. On your child's iPhone, open Settings and tap Sign
in to your iPhone at the top.
3. Don't type in an account. Tap Sign in a child in my
Family.
4. At Parent or Guardian Sign-In, sign in with your own
Apple Account.
5. At Which child will use this iPhone?, choose your
child and tap Continue. If they don't have an
account yet, tap Add Child to create one.
6. Follow the rest of the prompts.

svg.text: Turn on Screen Time and set
your code
5 minutes · on your child's phone
1. On your child's phone, open Settings and tap Screen
Time.
2. If Screen Time isn't on yet, turn it on.
3. Tap Lock Screen Time Settings (on some phones: Use
Screen Time Passcode).
4. Enter a four-digit code that your child does not
know, then enter it again.
5. When asked for an Apple Account for recovery, enter
your own, not your child's. This is how you get back
in if you forget the code.
This is the step people skip, and it's the reason
restrictions come off a fortnight later. Without a code,
your child can undo everything in about four taps.

svg.text: Allow only the apps on the
list
10 minutes · on your child's phone
1. Open Settings → Screen Time → App Limits → Add
Limit.
2. Tick these categories one by one: Social, Games,
Entertainment, Creativity, Productivity & Finance,
Education, Health & Fitness, Shopping & Food, Travel
and Other. Work down the list so you don't miss one.
3. Leave Information & Reading and Utilities unticked,
and don't tick Websites. Your child's phone needs
these two for getting on the web at all. The
websites step then limits the web to the sites on
the list.
4. Do not tick "All Apps & Categories" at the top. It
looks like a shortcut, but it also cuts off web
access, which undoes the websites step.
5. Tap Next and set the limit to 0 minutes.
6. Turn on Block at End of Limit. Without it there's an
"Ignore Limit" button and nothing holds.
7. Go back to Screen Time → Always Allowed.
8. The top section is what's allowed now: Phone,
Messages, FaceTime, Maps. Tap the red − on anything
that isn't on your list. Phone can't be removed.
9. The lower section lists everything else installed.
Tap the green + on each app on your list.
If an app on the list is blocked, check it's in the top
section of Always Allowed, not the lower one. If it still
won't open, email smartphonestudy@public.io. Don't remove
the category limit.

svg.text: Allow only the websites they
need
5 minutes · on your child's phone
1. Open Settings → Screen Time → Content & Privacy
Restrictions and turn it on.
2. Tap Allowed Apps & Features and make sure Safari is
on.
3. Go back, then tap App Store, Media, Web & Games →
Web Content.
4. Choose Only Approved Websites.
5. Swipe left to delete anything on the starter list
you don't want.
6. Tap Add Website and enter each site from the list,
exactly as written. A typo stops it working.
Check it works before you finish. Open Safari and load one
of the approved sites: it should open. Then type in a site
that isn't on the list, like youtube.com: it should be
blocked. If the blocked site loads, stop and email
smartphonestudy@public.io. Don't leave it as it is, because
your child would have an unrestricted browser, where they
could also reach the apps you just blocked.

svg.text: Lock the settings
3 minutes · on your child's phone
1. In Settings → Screen Time → Content & Privacy
Restrictions (already on from the last step), tap
iTunes & App Store Purchases.
2. Set Installing Apps, Deleting Apps and In-app
Purchases to Don't Allow.
3. Go back and scroll down to Allow Changes. Set
Passcode & Face ID and Accounts to Don't Allow.

g.text: Allow Apps to Request to Track

svg.text: Check it reached your phone
2 minutes · on your phone
1. On your phone, open Settings → Screen Time.
2. Your child's name should appear. Tap it.
3. You should see the settings you just made. If you
don't, check both phones are signed into the right
accounts and both are up to date.
